headline: Your Baicells waterfall journey.
subheadline: One routed cascade that finds operators and service providers with a live reason to build or upgrade RAN, and hands each one the Baicells proof that fits.
productSummary: Baicells Technologies sells disruptively priced 4G LTE and 5G NR access solutions: indoor and outdoor base stations (eNB/gNB), 4G and 5G CPEs, the Fusion RAN multi-mode platform (2G/4G/5G from one platform) and CloudCore, for mobile network extension, fixed wireless access, private and industrial networks (baicells.com).
coreInsight: Every RAN vendor pitches coverage and price. The operators who will actually buy are the ones with a public reason to spend on radio now: a fresh spectrum award or rollout obligation, a network still stuck on 2G/3G/4G, or a fixed-wireless business that lives or dies on cost per subscriber. Route on that reason, lead with 'Connect More with Less', and let the catch-all carry private-network and vertical buyers.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is a public reason to spend on radio access now
sections.takeaway: Spectrum awards, rollout obligations, legacy-only networks and fixed-wireless offers are all visible in regulator filings, operator websites and coverage data. No paid intent data needed.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: First match wins, top to bottom, catch-all underneath
sections.takeaway: Exclude existing Baicells customers and channel partners, then route: fresh spectrum award or rollout obligation, then no commercial 5G yet, then fixed-wireless / WISP operators, then every other operator, ISP and private-network buyer. Each account lands in exactly one campaign.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Four tiers, hottest to broadest
sections.takeaway: Pain comes from the trigger (coverage deadlines, 5G upgrade capex, cost per FWA subscriber). Value props come from baicells.com and Baicells press releases: disruptive pricing, software-upgradable 4G-to-5G radios, Fusion RAN, CPEs and private LTE/5G.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: One campaign per tier, one offer per campaign
sections.takeaway: CTOs and Heads of RAN / Network Planning get the capex and roadmap angle. FWA and WISP founders get the cost-per-subscriber angle. Enterprise buyers get the private-network angle.

sections.label: Emails
sections.title: Three-touch sequences, notice line first
sections.takeaway: Day 0 names the observed trigger, Day 3 rotates the value prop in-thread, Day 7 is the no-call ask: reply yes and we send the sheet. Proof lines come from baicells.com only.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Pull, route, send, then scale or cut on reply math
sections.takeaway: Build the operator and ISP TAM once for MEA and other emerging markets, run the routing agent, launch tiers with at least ~1,500 contacts, judge each on positive replies per send. Keep adding accounts; do not rebuild the strategy.

signalReasons: Spectrum awards, licence renewals and rollout obligations are published by national regulators, so a time-bound reason to buy radio is public and dated.
An operator's own site, press and coverage maps (Ookla, nPerf, GSMA coverage) show whether it has commercial 5G yet, which tells you if a 4G-to-5G upgrade story lands.
Fixed-wireless and WISP operators advertise FWA plans and coverage areas on their homepages, so the cost-per-subscriber pain is visible from a simple scrape.
All signals come with the TAM pull (regulator licence registries, operator directories, homepage scrape), so routing does not need expensive enrichment.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Spectrum award / rollout deadline
tiers.trigger: Operator or ISP received a 4G/5G spectrum award, licence renewal or coverage/rollout obligation from its regulator in the last 12 months.
tiers.pain: They now have to put radios on air in a fixed window, and incumbent-vendor RAN pricing makes hitting the coverage obligation expensive.
tiers.valueProp: Disruptively priced 4G LTE and 5G NR access solutions, plug-and-play design and low cost of entry (baicells.com); Fusion RAN runs multiple services (2G, 4G, 5G) from one platform (Baicells, Feb 2024).
tiers.magnet: Rollout cost sheet: coverage build for {{spectrum_band}} with Baicells outdoor base stations (operator plugs in its own site count)
tiers.dataSource: Regulator spectrum / licence registries + operator press
tiers.accounts: Estimate only; accumulate to ~1,500 contacts before launch

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: 5G upgrade path
tiers.trigger: MNO or ISP with no commercial 5G live yet (per its own site, press and coverage maps), not matched by Tier 1.
tiers.pain: They need a path to 5G but cannot justify ripping out existing 4G radios and paying for a full new RAN.
tiers.valueProp: Nova452 is a 4G eNodeB that upgrades to 5G by software without a hardware change; Fusion RAN supports 2G/4G/5G on one platform (Baicells press releases).
tiers.magnet: 4G-to-5G upgrade map: which of their current bands move to 5G by software on Baicells radios
tiers.dataSource: GSMA / operator press + Ookla / nPerf coverage data
tiers.replyDensity: High. Clear roadmap pain, no deadline (estimate)

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Fixed wireless economics
tiers.trigger: Operator advertises fixed-wireless / home-wireless plans or is a WISP, not matched by Tiers 1-2.
tiers.pain: Every new FWA subscriber needs base-station capacity and a CPE, so equipment cost per subscriber decides whether a rural or suburban area is profitable.
tiers.valueProp: Baicells supplies both 4G/5G base stations and 4G/5G CPEs for fixed wireless access, with plug-and-play design and low cost of entry (baicells.com).
tiers.magnet: FWA cost-per-subscriber sheet (base station + CPE), operator plugs in its own ARPU
tiers.dataSource: Homepage scrape + Google Maps ISP listings
tiers.replyDensity: Medium. Visible business model, no trigger (estimate)

tiers.name: Tier 4
tiers.label: Catch-all: private LTE/5G, connect more with less
tiers.trigger: Every remaining operator, ISP and enterprise / vertical account (mining, ports, oil and gas, utilities, transport, emergency services, campuses).
tiers.pain: Coverage gaps and unreliable Wi-Fi in large or remote sites, with private cellular assumed to be too expensive.
tiers.valueProp: Baicells solutions are deployed for M2M, IoT, transportation, emergency services, rural connectivity and deep indoor coverage, with private LTE deployments worldwide (baicells.com).
tiers.magnet: Private LTE/5G starter one-pager for {{vertical}} sites
tiers.dataSource: Regulator registries remainder + industry directories + Apollo

campaigns.strategy: Billboard opener on private LTE/5G for {{vertical}} sites, backed by Baicells footprint (1,400+ customers, 80+ countries), soft resource CTA.

launchPlan: Pull the TAM: licensed MNOs, ISPs and FWA operators from regulator registries in MEA and other emerging markets, plus WISPs from Google Maps and enterprise vertical accounts from industry directories.
Enrich once: regulator spectrum / obligation notices (last 12 months), commercial 5G status from operator press and coverage maps, homepage scrape for FWA plans.
Run the routing agent top to bottom: exclusions, Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3, catch-all. Assert every account exits with exactly one tier.
Find contacts via Apollo / Sales Navigator: CTO and Head of RAN / Network Planning at operators, founder at WISPs, IT/OT lead at enterprises.
Have Baicells approve the four offers (rollout cost sheet, upgrade map, FWA sheet, private-network one-pager) and every proof line before sends start.
Launch only tiers with ~1,500+ contacts. Tier 1 accumulates as awards publish; until it clears ~1,500, send those rows through Tier 2 copy.
Review reply math per tier after 1,500 sends, scale or cut per thresholds, then keep adding accounts without rebuilding the strategy.

thresholds.action: Cut the tier and re-route its leads to the catch-all
